key_insight: DDStereo aims to make stereo 3D road anomaly detection both fast enough for real-time use and robust to unseen objects. It does this with an efficient dual-decoder transformer design that targets the speed-accuracy tradeoff common in stereo methods.
problem_solved: The paper addresses two major safety challenges in stereo-based 3D detection: slow inference speed and weak open-set generalization to unknown road anomalies.
method: Introduces a dual-decoder transformer architecture for stereo 3D anomaly detection.
Optimizes the model for real-time efficiency while preserving the richer depth cues from stereo inputs.
Targets open-set road anomaly detection, helping the system handle objects or hazards not seen during training.
impact: This matters for autonomous driving and robotics because it brings stereo vision closer to practical deployment in safety-critical, real-time settings. For practitioners, it offers a path to better anomaly detection without relying on slower heavy models.

paper_title: DDStereo: Efficient Dual Decoder Transformers for Stereo 3D Road Anomaly Detection
paper_authors: Shiyi Mu, Zichong Gu, Zhiqi Ai, Yilin Gao, Shugong Xu
